text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Croatia unilaterally scraps visas for visitors from the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Israel.
- Foreign Minister Mate Granic and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright discuss in Washington the return of all refugees and the implementation of the Dayton peace accord.
- Croatian government decides to ban weekend lorry traffic during the tourist season.

- The largest Croatian banks own shares in hotels along the Adriatic. The second round of hotel sell-off is expected as soon as the Privatisation Fund distributes the tourist portfolio in voucher privatisation.
- The Korean Daewoo concern is holding talks with several state institutions on investing into the Dubrovnik Babin Kuk hotels.
- Zagreb's heatwave on Thursday: Some 32 degrees Celsius in the shade and 50 degrees in the sun!
- The Lobor international festival of off-road racing to take place over the weekend some 45 kilometers north-east of Zagreb.
- A group of experts from the Japanese Institute for Overseas Investment (JOI) holds talks with the head of the Craotian Investment Promotion Agency Vanja Kalogjera on possible future cooperation.
- The budding Croatian tennis star Mirjana Lucic splits with her coach of six months Goran Prpic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
